version.changelog: Replace .env loading with config.json fallback for client creds

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: withings-family
Version: 1.0.4

The skill is designed to fetch health data from the Withings API for multiple family members. All code and documentation align with this stated purpose. Key security features include robust input sanitization for user IDs (`scripts/withings.py`, `scripts/withings_oauth_local.py`) to prevent path traversal, secure file permissions (0o600) for token storage, and all network communication directed exclusively to the legitimate Withings API (`https://wbsapi.withings.net`). The OAuth flow in `scripts/withings_oauth_local.py` correctly uses a `state` parameter for CSRF protection. There is no evidence of data exfiltration to unauthorized endpoints, malicious execution, persistence mechanisms, obfuscation, or prompt injection attempts against the agent in the markdown files.

llm.summary: The skill's code, required environment variables, and runtime instructions are consistent with a Withings API client for multiple users; nothing in the files suggests hidden exfiltration or unrelated privileges, though there are a few minor documentation vs code inconsistencies you should be aware of.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (Withings family data) matches the actual code and required secrets: the scripts only talk to Withings endpoints and ask for WITHINGS_CLIENT_ID and WITHINGS_CLIENT_SECRET. Required binary (python3) is appropriate.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions and the CLI map to the scripts' behaviors (OAuth, token storage, per-user token files, data fetch commands). Minor mismatches: SKILL.md and README mention storing creds in a .env file under ~/.openclaw/withings-family/.env, but both scripts look for config.json in that directory (they read BASE_DIR/config.json) or environment variables — the .env suggestion is inaccurate. Another small doc mismatch: one file header references localhost:8080 while the code and all documentation use port 18081. These are documentation inconsistencies but not malicious scope creep. Scripts only access files under ~/.openclaw/withings-family (or legacy path) and do not read other system secrets.

dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec; this is instruction + included Python scripts that use only the standard library. Nothing is downloaded or extracted at install time.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests only WITHINGS_CLIENT_ID and WITHINGS_CLIENT_SECRET, which are exactly what an OAuth client needs. It does not ask for additional unrelated credentials or broad config paths. Tokens are stored locally per-user; the code attempts to set file mode 600.

dimensions.detail: always:false and the skill does not request elevated privileges or modify other skills. It stores tokens in a dedicated directory under the user's home; that is expected and scoped to the skill.

llm.guidance: This skill looks coherent for accessing Withings data and only needs your Withings client ID/secret. Before installing or running: 1) Verify the Github source (homepage) if you don't already trust the author; review the two included scripts to confirm there are no changes. 2) Prefer setting WITHINGS_CLIENT_ID and WITHINGS_CLIENT_SECRET as environment variables rather than putting secrets into files that might be accidentally committed. 3) Be aware tokens are saved under ~/.openclaw/withings-family/tokens-<user>.json (the code tries to set permissions to 600) — protect that directory. 4) Note minor doc inconsistencies (.env vs config.json, stray comment about port 8080); the actual scripts use a local callback on port 18081. 5) Run the OAuth helper in a local/isolated environment and ensure no unexpected process is binding the callback port. If you want extra caution, inspect the two scripts line-by-line or run them inside a container or VM before using with real credentials.
